No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Arsenal’s Resilience Can Inspire Nigeria’s Renewal, Says Atiku by Kunle Olasanmi 2 minutes ago in Sport , Football Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has said the resilience associated with English football club Arsenal could inspire Nigeria’s quest for national renewal and a brighter future.
Atiku, represented by Senator Dino Melaye, spoke at the inauguration of Arsenal Fans Club Nigeria in Abuja, where he urged Nigerians to draw inspiration from the club’s fighting spirit in overcoming the country’s challenges.
He likened the country’s struggles to the biblical promise that weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning.
“By the grace of God, very soon, Nigerians will leave the wilderness and enter the Promised Land,” he said.
Atiku congratulated the club’s National President, Charles Ojugbana, and others behind the initiative, describing the inauguration as a historic event.
He also pledged his support for the organisation, expressing hope that the resilience associated with Arsenal would inspire Nigerians and contribute to restoring the country’s lost glory.
Earlier, Ojugbana unveiled a three-tier expansion plan aimed at growing the club’s membership and promoting Arsenal’s values across the country.
He said the first phase would focus on establishing chapters nationwide, adding that four state chapters in Gombe, Imo, Lagos and Akwa Ibom had been inaugurated at the club’s annual general meeting.
According to him, the club plans to establish chapters in all 36 states by the end of 2027 before expanding into tertiary institutions and major cities.
“Every university in Nigeria will have an Arsenal Fans Club, and then we will move to the cities. In the next two years, we intend to have five million registered Nigerians in this club,” he said.
Ojugbana said the initiative would promote excellence, discipline and Arsenal’s style of football while providing a platform for supporting players of Nigerian descent making their mark abroad.
He cited Arsenal players Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke, Bukayo Saka and Ethan Nwaneri as examples of footballers whose Nigerian connections could strengthen the club’s appeal among supporters in the country.
Describing Arsenal supporters as committed and well-behaved, he urged fans of rival clubs to embrace friendly competition rather than envy the Gunners.
The Chairman of the Board of Trustees, Ambassador Adamu Emozozo, who addressed the gathering virtually, urged members to remain united and committed to building an organisation that future generations would be proud to inherit.
The chairman of the occasion described the inauguration as symbolic, saying it celebrated not only a football club but also the values of love, perseverance, hope, courage and determination.
Also speaking, Dalhatu Musa, Accord Party senatorial candidate for the Federal Capital Territory, said the club was founded on the belief that football could unite people across racial and social divides.
Musa noted that Arsenal supporters remained committed to their team regardless of its performance, adding that such resilience could extend beyond football into other aspects of their lives.
He urged members to embrace sportsmanship, stressing that winning and losing were integral parts of the game.
“You win some and lose some, but you must have the spirit of sportsmanship. Win or lose, we are always good,” he said.
Musa also called on the government, corporate organisations and wealthy individuals to increase investment in football and other sports to develop young talents.
He lamented the decline of grassroots sporting initiatives, citing the Minister’s Cup in the FCT, which he said had previously provided opportunities for emerging talents.
“Government needs to invest heavily in sports and, after investing, sit back and reap the benefit of what it has sown,” he said.
He called for the revival of grassroots competitions and the creation of an enabling environment to attract greater private-sector investment in sports.
The highlight of the inauguration was the investiture and induction of patrons, with Atiku named Grand Patron of the club.
Other patrons include the Emir of Kano, Sanusi Lamido Sanusi; Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke; business mogul Aliko Dangote; former Senate President Bukola Saraki; Melaye; and former Imo State Governor Emeka Ihedioha.
Former Super Eagles captain Nwankwo Kanu was also named a patron and brand ambassador of the organisation.
